result.title: Recovering from Pose-Selection Failures in Repeated Visual Localization
result.summary: Repetitive structures can give an incorrect pose candidate more inlier support than an accurate one, causing visual localization to select it. History-Guided Pose Reselection (HPR) uses coarse position forecasts from up to five past localization outputs to distinguish well-separated current-query candidates. The best-fitting forecast proposes an alternative; HPR accepts it only if every well-fitting forecast is much closer to it than to the localizer's pose. HPR needs no odometry and returns the selected candidate unchanged, using prediction for selection rather than pose refinement. With one development-set threshold, HPR improves recall within 5 meters and 10 degrees in all 12 main configurations of Hierarchical Localization (HLoc), MASt3R-based pose generation, and JIST-based retrieval, losing successes on fewer than 0.4 percent of queries. On NAVER Gangnam B1, HPR corrects 97 HLoc failures and loses six successes; gains persist within 0.25 meters and 2 degrees on all three HLoc test sets. Median HPR runtime on HLoc candidates is below one millisecond, excluding pose generation. Recovery weakens under less frequent localization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 History-Guided Pose Reselection（HPR）：用最近至多五次定位输出做粗略位置预测，当某个候选被所有预测一致支持时，才替换定位器选择的位姿，从而缓解重复结构导致的错误候选被选中问题，并在 HLoc、MASt3R、JIST 等配置上提升召回。
AI.relevance_reason: 把历史输出当作隐式信念状态来校验候选、仅在多源预测一致时才接受的保守决策方式，可能为 LVR 中的候选筛选与停止/接受判据提供线索，但其非多模态、非 latent 生成，具体可迁移性仍需核查。
